A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

relations.definition: Indicates a future state or condition of an entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: will be in: Indicates a future state or condition of an entity.

chosen_property.label: willBeInAgeRange
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a future age range that a person will be in.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly represents a future age range for a person.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: itemCondition
candidates.comment: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: orderStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: stage
candidates.comment: A classification of a medical condition by its applicable stage. Also called "condition stage", "disease stage", "progression stage". Examples: "The cancer has stage Stage III", "The medical condition's stage is early", "This disease is in stage 2."

relations.definition: Indicates a formal agreement between two entities.
relations.embedding_query_text: has contract with: Indicates a formal agreement between two entities.

chosen_property.label: worksFor
chosen_property.justification: A SportsClub is an Organization, and 'worksFor' accurately describes a person having a contract with an organization.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: acceptedOffer
candidates.comment: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."

candidates.label: broker
candidates.comment: An intermediary relation between an invoice, order, reservation, or service and the organization or person who arranges the exchange. Also called "arranged by", "intermediary", "agent". Examples: "Flight reservation broker Expedia", "Real estate service broker John Doe", "Stock order broker Fidelity". Distinct from seller or buyer, which indicate direct parties in an exchange, whereas broker facilitates it without taking ownership.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: termsOfService
candidates.comment: A textual or URL reference to the human-readable terms of service documentation for a service. Also called "service agreement", "user agreement", "terms and conditions", "legal terms". Examples: "The online service has termsOfService a link to its policy", "The software's termsOfService are available on its website", "This service requires agreement to its termsOfService."

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

relations.definition: Specifies the ending year of a duration or agreement.
relations.embedding_query_text: until year: Specifies the ending year of a duration or agreement.

chosen_property.label: contractedUntilYear
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the calendar year until which a contract or agreement with an entity is valid.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links a SportsClub to a CalendarYear for the end of a contract or agreement.

candidates.label: leaseLength
candidates.comment: A rental term relation between an accommodation, offer, or real estate listing and the duration of its lease agreement. Also called lease duration, rental period, term of lease, tenancy length. Examples: An accommodation has a leaseLength of '12 months'. An offer specifies a leaseLength of '2 years'. A real estate listing has a leaseLength of '6-month minimum'. Distinct from duration, which is a general duration for any event or item.

candidates.label: loanTerm
candidates.comment: A loan duration relation between a loan or credit and the quantitative value representing its agreement term. Also called: loan duration, credit term, repayment period. Examples: "Car Loan loanTerm '60 months'", "Mortgage loanTerm '30 years'", "Personal Loan loanTerm '5 years'".

candidates.label: billingDuration
candidates.comment: A duration, number, or quantitative value specifying how long a price or price component will be billed. Also called: billing period length, contractual duration, payment plan length. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Subscription' billingDuration 'P1Y' (1 year)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Service Plan' billingDuration '12' (months)."

candidates.label: expires
candidates.comment: An expiration relation between a certification or creative work and the date or datetime when its validity, usefulness, or availability ends. Also called: valid until, end date, availability end. Examples: "Software License" expires "2024-12-31", "News Article" expires "2023-10-30T23:59:59", "Professional Certification" expires "2025-06-01".

candidates.label: validThrough
candidates.comment: A valid through relation between a demand, financial incentive, job posting, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, or opening hours specification and the date after which it is no longer valid. Also called expiration date, end date, valid until. Examples: "Offer validThrough '2023-12-31'", "JobPosting validThrough '2023-11-30'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validThrough '2024-12-31'". Distinct from validFrom, which specifies the start of validity. Distinct from validUntil, which is similar but for Permit only.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: validUntil
candidates.comment: A valid until relation between a permit and the date it ceases to be valid. Also called permit expiration date, permit end date, validity end date. Examples: "Permit validUntil '2024-06-30'", "Permit validUntil '2025-01-01'", "Permit validUntil '2023-12-31'". Distinct from validThrough, which is a more general property for various items.

candidates.label: priceValidUntil
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date after which an offered price is no longer valid or available. Also called offer expiry date, price expiration, valid until date. Examples: An offer has a price valid until '2023-12-31'. The discount price is valid until 'next month'. The special offer's price valid until is '2024-01-15'.

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

candidates.label: yearBuilt
candidates.comment: A construction year relation between an accommodation and a number, indicating the year in which the accommodation was built. Also called construction year, built year, year of construction. Examples: Hotel yearBuilt 1985, ApartmentBuilding yearBuilt 2010, House yearBuilt 1950.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo

candidates.label: relatedTo

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: about

Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: statType

Also called "statistic type", "measurement type", "data type", "statistical measure". Examples: "The variable has statType mean", "This statistical variable's statType is count", "The statType indicates a median value."

candidates.label: programType
candidates.comment: A program type relation between an educational or occupational program and its classification or format. Also called type of program, program format, program category. Examples: "A university course is of program type 'classroom'.", "A medical residency is of program type 'internship'.", "A vocational training is of program type 'apprenticeship'."

candidates.label: legislationType

Examples: "GDPR legislationType regulation", "Civil Rights Act legislationType law", "EU Directive legislationType directive".

candidates.label: structuralClass

Examples: "The knee joint has structuralClass synovial", "The skull sutures have structuralClass fibrous", "This joint's structuralClass is cartilaginous."

candidates.label: loanType
candidates.comment: A loan type relation between a loan or credit and its specific category. Also called: credit type, loan category, financing type. Examples: "Home Loan loanType 'Mortgage'", "Student Loan loanType 'Federal Student Loan'", "Business Loan loanType 'SBA Loan'".

candidates.label: priceType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute defining the specific type of a price, such as a list price, sale price, or manufacturer suggested retail price. The product's price type is 'MSRP'.

candidates.label: fuelType
candidates.comment: A fuel type relation between an engine specification or vehicle and the kind of fuel it is designed to use. Also called: energy source, power type, fuel kind. Examples: "Gasoline Engine" fuel type "Unleaded Gasoline", "Diesel Truck" fuel type "Diesel", "Electric Car" fuel type "Electricity".

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: genre
candidates.comment: A genre relation between a broadcast channel, creative work, or music group and its category or style. Also called: category, style, type. Examples: "Novel '1984'" genre "Dystopian Fiction", "BBC News" genre "News", "Rock Band 'Queen'" genre "Rock".

candidates.label: exerciseType

Examples: "Morning Run" exercise type "Aerobics", "Weightlifting Session" exercise type "Strength Training", "Yoga Practice" exercise type "Flexibility Training".
